launches.name: Eclipse Enclave (enclave.eclipse.dev)
launches.desc: Eclipse Foundation open-source sandbox: every coding-agent session gets its own container, filesystem view, and network gateway. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and others run with permission prompts off because the sandbox — not the human — is the gate.
launches.why: The brief is about who may run a cyber model. Enclave answers the local version: what the agent on your laptop is allowed to touch.

launches.name: Harden AIF (harden.run)
launches.desc: A free, local firewall for coding agents. A post-trained cybersecurity model checks each tool call against your intent and session context, then allows, rewrites, asks, or blocks — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and others. Repo and tool output stay on the machine.
launches.why: Same week Google gated Flash Cyber behind Fairwind. Harden is the desk-level check: the agent does not get a free pass on rm, npx, or your keys.

launches.name: Cadenya (cadenya.com)
launches.desc: A hosted agentic loop rather than a framework you bolt on. Connect OpenAPI and MCP tools; Cadenya runs context compaction, tool approvals, webhooks, and streaming. Model-agnostic via OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
launches.why: The missing harness people keep rewriting: tool calls, compaction, and an approval gate as a service — not another closed managed-agents box.

launches.name: Elva (getelva.ai)
launches.desc: Discovers APIs in your repo, writes audience contracts, and hosts MCP servers behind scoped keys, per-tool auth, and full call logs. Built for the week when agents — not only developers — are the API consumers.
launches.why: The Anthropic report treats stolen AI keys as loot. Elva issues keys per agent and revokes them in one click — the MCP equivalent of not leaving AWS keys in the APK.

quotes.who: Zhen Lu, Runpod CEO — on 'model fatigue'
quotes.text: The pace is disorienting IT buyers. Nobody wants to be the lab standing still, so everyone ships — and the people who have to evaluate all of it can't keep up with the scoreboard.

quotes.who: Aakash Gupta, product analyst — on the Hugging Face deal
quotes.text: Nvidia spent 12 days of revenue to make sure the open-source rival to its own customers never dies.

quotes.who: Peder, Blume co-founder — Product Hunt launch
quotes.text: We tried to control agent drift with all the best practices: rules, skills, docs, self-verification. But when our repo grew, the setup rotted fast. Manual maintenance is too time consuming, and asking the agent to maintain it led to context drift and bloat.

trends.title: Safeguard tiers are becoming the unit of release
trends.desc: Anthropic shipped the same model at two tiers (Fable public, Mythos gated). Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash plus a looser-mitigation 'Cyber' variant behind its Fairwind Program. OpenAI restricted Astra's cyber capabilities to 'trusted defenders.' Three labs in one week chose to differentiate on who gets access rather than on what the model does — the natural endgame after OpenAI's own agents breached Hugging Face in July.

trends.title: The agent layer just got a security layer
trends.desc: Eclipse Enclave sandboxes the session. Harden checks the tool call before it runs. Elva scopes the MCP key. None of these are agents — they are the sandbox, firewall, and API gate that appear once agents have production credentials to steal.
